source: M. A. Hupfauf, Secondary debris resulting from concrete slabs subjected to contact detonations, PhD thesis, Universitaet der Bundeswehr Muenchen, 2024 (athene-forschung.unibw.de/149703); and M. Hupfauf and N. Gebbeken, Advances in Structural Engineering 25(7) (2022) 1373-1385, doi:10.1177/13694332221080614
licence: CC BY 4.0. Derived data: values transcribed from the thesis's tables 4.1-4.4 and read off its figures 4.11, 4.13, 4.17, 4.20, 4.21 and 4.22; see README.md.

slab.bars: B500B, 10 mm at 150 mm both ways in both faces, 35 mm cover

chargeNote: Cylinders 103 mm across, one end flush with the slab, initiated about 10 mm into the far end. The spherical factor gives the sphere of the same energy-equivalent impulse (thesis section 3.3).
groupNote: Within a group the order of the values follows the shots only where the thesis names them (SN82, SN143-SN147 in figure 4.17; SN174, SN144, SN147 and SN131 in figures 4.18 and 4.21); elsewhere it is the order read off the figure. Diameters are of the area-equivalent circle on the protective face; debris mass is the spall crater's scanned volume times the density.

crushingCrater.note: Figure 4.11, by TNT-spherical mass in g; includes the four slabs with a retrofitted layer on the protective face (SN154, SN155, SN161, SN162), which the thesis treats as plain on the loaded side.

fits.profile: v(r) = vxMax (0.25 L + 0.75 G), L = Gamma^2 / (Gamma^2 + r^2), G = exp(-r^2 / (2 sigma^2)), Gamma = sigma / 2

rigidLoadReference.note: Total impulse on a rigid surface 0.1 ms after the detonation of 1500 g of SEMTEX 10, a cylinder 100 mm across and 120 mm long (L/D 1.2) in contact, from S-ALE simulations with JWL products extrapolated to zero cell size (thesis section 3.2).
